issues.t: Timing chain guides can break
issues.sym: A whine that rises with engine speed, a rattle at start-up, low oil pressure warnings, misfires or a drivetrain malfunction message.
issues.why: The plastic guides for the timing chain turn brittle and break. Pieces fall into the oil pan and the chain can jump, wrecking the engine. BMW revised the parts in 2015 and a class action extended coverage on early engines.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear a new whine or rattle and have the chain and guides inspected. Ask a dealer whether the settlement coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Coolant pump connector can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often nothing. Possibly a burning smell, smoke from under the hood or a coolant pump fault.
issues.why: The plug on the electric water pump may not be sealed. Moisture can get in and cause a short circuit, even when parked.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for recall 24V-608 and have it done free. Park outside until the repair is complete.

issues.t: Crankcase vent valve heater can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Possibly a burning plastic smell or smoke from the engine bay, even with the car parked.
issues.why: A small heater on the crankcase ventilation valve can short circuit and melt nearby parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for recall 17V-683 and have the heater replaced free. Park outside until then.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor mat cracks and turns the airbag off
issues.sym: The airbag warning light or the passenger airbag off light stays on with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The sensing mat inside the front passenger seat cushion can crack from people getting in and out, so the car no longer detects a passenger.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 08V-384 and 17V-605 and have the mat replaced. Until then, the passenger airbag may not work in a crash.

issues.t: Transfer case and its actuator motor wear out
issues.sym: Whining or grinding from under the middle of the car, jerking or binding in tight turns, and 4x4, ABS and brake warning lights together.
issues.why: The small motor that controls the all-wheel-drive clutch has a plastic gear that wears, and the transfer case chain and clutch can wear too, especially with mismatched tires or old fluid.
issues.next: Have the fault codes read soon. Often only the actuator motor or its gear needs replacing if caught early. Keep all four tires matched.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the oil filter housing and valve cover gaskets
issues.sym: Burning oil smell, oil on the front or side of the engine, drips on the ground and low oil messages.
issues.why: The rubber gaskets harden with heat. A leaking filter housing gasket can also soak the drive belt in oil, and a slipping belt can get pulled into the engine.
issues.next: Have leaks fixed soon, especially at the oil filter housing, and replace an oil-soaked belt at the same time.

issues.t: Electric water pump or thermostat fails
issues.sym: Temperature warning, cooling fan running flat out, reduced power or a check engine light for the thermostat.
issues.why: The electric coolant pump can stop without warning, and the electronically controlled thermostat is a frequent failure too.
issues.next: Pull over and switch off if the red temperature warning shows. Have the pump and thermostat replaced together.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from the expansion tank, hoses and plastic fittings
issues.sym: Low coolant warning, a sweet smell, or pink or blue drips under the front of the car.
issues.why: Plastic cooling parts such as the expansion tank and hose connectors get brittle with heat cycles and crack.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the system pressure-tested soon. Do not drive it if the temperature warning comes on.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may be defective (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The defect only matters if the airbag deploys in a crash.
issues.why: A manufacturing fault in some driver airbag inflators can make them burst when the airbag fires.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 16V-683 and 23V-797 and have the driver airbag replaced free as soon as possible.

issues.t: Front swivel bearings may not be hardened properly (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly no warning, or clunking and loose, wandering steering from the front end.
issues.why: Some front swivel bearings (the knuckles that carry the front wheels) skipped proper heat treatment and can break.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V-678 and have the parts replaced free before driving much further.

issues.t: Rear brake hoses may leak (recall)
issues.sym: Brake warning light, a soft or longer pedal, or fluid near a rear wheel.
issues.why: Rear brake hoses on some new-generation X3s can leak, cutting rear braking and disabling ABS and stability control.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check the VIN for recall 25V-154 and have the hoses replaced free. Do not drive with a brake warning or a soft pedal.

issues.t: Starter motor can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning smell from the engine bay, slow or no cranking, or smoke with the car switched off.
issues.why: The starter can keep drawing current and overheat, which can set nearby parts alight even when the car is parked.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for this recall and have the starter replaced free. Until then park outside and away from buildings.

issues.t: Starter relay can corrode and short out (recall)
issues.sym: Burning plastic smell, blown fuses, odd electrical faults, or no crank.
issues.why: Moisture can corrode the starter relay so it shorts, and the heat from that short is a fire risk even when the car sits unused.
issues.next: Have the relay replaced free under the recall. BMW told owners to park outside until the work is done.

issues.t: Steering shaft may be wrongly attached to the column (recall)
issues.sym: Play or a loose feel in the wheel, a clicking or clunking as you turn, or a steering warning message.
issues.why: The shaft that joins the wheel to the steering gear may not have been fitted correctly at the factory, so it can work loose.
issues.next: Stop driving if the wheel feels loose or disconnected, and have the car inspected free under the recall.

issues.t: Steering wheel can turn by itself while the car sits still (recall)
issues.sym: The wheel moves on its own when the car is stopped or parked, with no input from you.
issues.why: A software fault in the steering control can command a small movement when the car is stationary, which can catch your hands or a bystander.
issues.next: Have the free software update done. Keep hands clear of the wheel rim if it has moved on its own.

issues.t: Rear door locks can release in one movement (recall)
issues.sym: A rear door that should be locked opens from the inside on the first pull of the handle.
issues.why: The second-row lock can unlatch in a single motion instead of needing the lock released first, so a child could open a door while driving.
issues.next: Have the lock parts replaced free under the recall. Use the child lock switch in the meantime if your car has one.

issues.t: Cargo rail anchors can tear loose in a rear crash (recalls)
issues.sym: Nothing in normal use. The rails in the load floor may feel loose if the anchor has already pulled.
issues.why: The anchor points for the cargo rails were not strong enough, so luggage tied to them could come free in a rear impact.
issues.next: Check the VIN: two campaigns cover this and the repair may be covered. Do not tie heavy loads to the rails until it is done.

issues.t: Transmission control unit can leak oil and lock up a gear (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission warning message, harsh or stuck shifts, or a sudden jolt and loss of drive.
issues.why: A weld in the transmission control unit can let oil escape, and that can make the gearbox seize in gear.
issues.next: Have it checked under the recall before driving far. A gear that locks up at speed can make the car hard to control.

issues.t: Steering gear mounting bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Vague or loose steering, a knock from the front end when turning, or wandering at speed.
issues.why: The bolts holding the steering gear may not have been tightened properly, so the gear can shift on its mounts.
issues.next: Have the bolts inspected and tightened free under the recall. Do not keep driving with loose-feeling steering.

issues.t: Camshaft timing unit bolts can loosen and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, a rattle from the front of the engine, or a stall with no warning.
issues.why: Bolts in the variable valve timing unit can work loose or break, which upsets valve timing and can shut the engine down.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have this done under the recall. A stall in traffic is dangerous, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Diesel exhaust gas cooler can leak and melt the intake (recalls)
issues.sym: Coolant loss with no puddle, a sweet or burning smell, white smoke, or engine warning lights.
issues.why: The cooler for recirculated exhaust gas can crack and leak coolant into hot exhaust gas, which can melt the plastic intake and start a fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN: two campaigns cover this and the repair may be covered. Stop driving if you smell burning or lose coolant.

issues.t: Diesel high-pressure fuel pump can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Long cranking, a stumble or loss of power, then a stall and a car that will not restart.
issues.why: The high-pressure pump can wear internally and stop feeding the injectors, which shuts the engine off without warning.
issues.next: Have it checked under the recall. A stall at speed on a highway is a real safety risk.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid battery can short out and catch fire (recalls)
issues.sym: Hybrid system warnings, a sharp or burning smell, or much less electric range than usual.
issues.why: Debris and stray welding material left inside the high-voltage battery can bridge cells and start a fire, even while charging or parked.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Two campaigns cover this and the work may be covered. BMW told owners not to charge and to park outside until it is fixed.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel rail can crack and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: Strong fuel smell, a hard start or rough idle, and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: The rail that holds fuel at high pressure for the injectors can crack, and petrol sprayed in a hot engine bay is a fire risk.
issues.next: Do not drive with a fuel smell. Have the rail replaced free under the recall.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper pistons may be poorly coated (recall)
issues.sym: A longer pedal, weaker braking than you expect, or the stability control warning coming on while braking hard.
issues.why: The piston coating in the rear calipers can let gas form in the fluid under heavy braking, which cuts rear braking.
issues.next: Have the calipers replaced free under the recall, and get the brakes looked at now if stopping feels poor.

issues.t: Front seat back frame welds can let the seat fold (recall)
issues.sym: A seat back that feels loose, moves more than it should, or suddenly tips back.
issues.why: Welds joining the seat back frame to the rails may be incomplete, so the back can collapse in a crash or under load.
issues.next: Have the seat frame replaced free under the recall. Do not let anyone ride in a seat whose back moves on its own.

issues.t: Backup camera view can be blocked or go blank (recalls)
issues.sym: The reversing picture is missing, frozen, partly hidden, or the screen stays dark when you select reverse.
issues.why: Display settings and camera software could hide part of the image or leave the screen blank, so you cannot see what is behind you.
issues.next: Check the VIN: several campaigns cover this with a software update. It may be covered. Keep using mirrors and look over your shoulder.

issues.t: Steering tie rod can fracture on the X3 M (recall)
issues.sym: A knock or shimmy from the front, steering that pulls or feels loose, or sudden loss of control of one wheel.
issues.why: A tie rod in the steering gear can break, and a broken tie rod leaves that front wheel steering itself.
issues.next: Have it inspected under the recall before driving the car hard, and stop driving if the steering feels wrong.

issues.t: Left front wheel carrier can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking or creaking from the left front, uneven tire wear, or steering that wanders.
issues.why: The left front wheel carrier may not have been made to strength, so it can crack and in the worst case break apart.
issues.next: Have it replaced free under the recall. Do not keep driving with a new knock from the front suspension.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump can fail and stiffen the pedal (recalls)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal that needs much more effort, sometimes after the car has sat overnight.
issues.why: The pump that provides brake boost can run short of lubrication and seize, which takes away power assist and lengthens stopping distance.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for these campaigns and have the pump replaced. Treat a suddenly hard pedal as urgent.

issues.t: Power steering assist can cut out suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: The wheel goes heavy without warning, usually with a steering warning light.
issues.why: The electric power steering control module can fault and drop assist, which makes the car much harder to turn at low speed.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have the steering module dealt with under the recall, and park the car if assist drops out while driving.
